open_questions: OWL footprint: 15.3 GW / 'more than 140 data centers owned or under construction' (Q2 call, 2026-07-30) vs 'almost 14 GW' / 'over 130 data centers operational or under construction' (Q3 call, 2026-10-29). No reconciliation and no GW basis (facility vs IT load); the two definitions also differ ('owned' vs 'operational'). Both quotes carry the Kirshenbaum label in the MarketBeat/Quartr transcripts; the timeline does not name a speaker.

Cost per GW: Fink ~$50bn per 1 GW including chips (40% chips, BLK 2026-10-14) vs Lipschultz ~$15bn per GW excluding chips (OWL 2026-10-29). Even ex-chips, Fink's 60% implies ~$30bn/GW (Capstone arithmetic), about 2x Lipschultz. Neither states a GW basis; neither replaces the canonical $/GW in _meta/assumptions.md.

Meta RVG attribution: Air Street (2026-10-08) lists 'Meta $41bn (Hyperion)'. Meta's 3Q 10-Q (filed 2026-10-22) shows $41.493bn maximum RVG across BOTH ventures (Louisiana + Texas) vs $28.091bn at 2025-12-31 (Louisiana only). The $41bn should not be attributed to the Blue Owl/Hyperion JV alone.

Hyperion amount bases: Lipschultz '$30 billion of capital investment' (2025-10-30) vs Meta 10-Q 'approximately $27 billion' development cost vs ~$28.8bn capital base (Global Data Center Hub, workbook facility cost) vs ~$27.3bn notes. Distribution to Meta: $2.6bn (10-Q) vs ~$3bn (release relay). Whether the 5 GW expansion sits inside the notes' perimeter is unknown.

Texas Venture: the TXEDCI dossier (as of 2026-10-16) says no filing confirms closing; Meta's 3Q 10-Q (filed 2026-10-22) now says Meta holds 20% 'following the closing' ($2.26bn contributed, $1.04bn distribution).
